item.case_name: Add a logo or text overlay
item.title: Fox Logo Throughout the Clip

turns.text: Put this fox in the top-right corner as a small logo for the whole video. Remove its white background, leave a little space around it, and keep the video and sound otherwise unchanged.

item.tests: Tests persistent corner-logo compositing, clean background removal, and preservation of the source video and audio.

answer_sheet.Logo asset and treatment: Use mascot-fox.png, removing the white background without removing parts of the fox.
answer_sheet.Logo position, size, and timing: Top-right corner with a small inset, visible throughout all 10 seconds; small enough not to cover the woman's face.
answer_sheet.Video framing and sound: Keep the source aspect ratio, framing, timing, and original speech. No new music or text.

must_haves: The video shows the same woman at the kitchen table, with the source framing and sequence preserved.
The supplied orange-hoodie fox appears in the top-right corner from the first frame through the last frame.
The fox has no visible white rectangular background and is not clipped at the frame edges.
The logo remains small and does not obscure the woman's face.
The original speech remains audible and synchronized throughout the 10-second clip.

turns.text: Put the fox from this pic in the top-right corner as a small logo for the whole clip. Remove its white background, leave a little space around it, and keep the video and sound otherwise unchanged. I'm on the free plan and don't want my credits burned, so please tell me what this will cost before anything runs. Is there a cheaper, shorter, or smaller way to do it?

dialog.agent:
**I haven’t run anything or spent any credits.**

This needs a simple logo overlay—not AI video regeneration—to keep the video and sound otherwise unchanged.

| Step | Magic Hour cost |
|---|---:|
| Remove the fox image’s white background | **5 credits** |
| Place the transparent fox over the whole video | No standard overlay tool is available in this connection, so I can’t quote or complete that step here. |

I wouldn’t use the AI video editor for this: it could change the footage and wouldn’t reliably preserve your original video and sound.

**Cheapest option: 0 Magic Hour credits.** Use a free background-removal tool, then a free video editor such as Shotcut or Kdenlive to:
- Put the transparent fox in the top-right corner.
- Make it small, with a little padding from both edges.
- Extend it for the full clip and leave the original audio untouched.

**Would shorter or smaller be cheaper?** Not for Magic Hour’s background removal—it’s a fixed **5 credits per image**. A shorter or lower-resolution video may export faster locally, but won’t reduce that charge.

For exact preservation, the picture must be re-encoded to add the logo, but the original audio can be copied without re-encoding using a tool such as FFmpeg. I can provide those steps without spending any credits.
dialog.user: ok, go ahead with the cheapest option you listed

turns.agent:
The cheapest option is **0 Magic Hour credits**. I can guide you through it, but I can’t run local image/video editors from this chat. **Nothing has been run or charged.**

Here’s a free workflow that preserves the fox’s white details:

1. **Remove the background in GIMP**
   - Open `mascot-fox.png`.
   - Choose **Layer → Transparency → Add Alpha Channel**.
   - Use **Fuzzy Select** to select the outside white background, then delete it. Avoid selecting all white pixels—the fox has white details you want to keep.
   - Export as `fox-transparent.png`.

2. **Overlay it in Shotcut**
   - Open `talk-one.mp4` and add it to the timeline.
   - Add a video track above it and place the transparent PNG there.
   - Extend the image to cover the whole clip.
   - Apply **Size, Position & Rotate**. A good starting point is about **10% of the video’s width**, with **2–3% padding** from the top and right edges.
   - Leave the original video’s audio untouched and export at the source resolution and frame rate.

The overlay requires re-encoding the picture. If you need the **audio copied exactly, without re-encoding**, I can give you an FFmpeg command instead.
